									<p data-pm-slice="1 1 []">Nigeria’s Super Eagles will face Russia in Tuesday’s international friendly with a significantly depleted squad after injuries and club restrictions ruled several invited players out of the encounter. The absences have reduced Head Coach Éric Chelle’s options and placed greater emphasis on squad depth as Nigeria prepares for a demanding international assignment.</p>
<p>Captain Wilfred Ndidi is among the notable absentees after sustaining a minor knock during Nigeria’s 2027 Africa Cup of Nations qualifier against Guinea-Bissau last week. His absence removes one of the team’s most experienced midfield options and leaves Chelle with fewer established players to rely on in the centre of the pitch.</p>
<p>The situation was compounded by the decision of Eintracht Frankfurt not to release midfielder Raphael Onyedika for the friendly. Defender Bright Osayi-Samuel and UAE-based midfielder Ridwan Abdulrasaq Popoola were also prevented by their clubs from joining the national team.</p>
<p>Switzerland-based defender Victory Akpe will miss the trip because of an injury, further limiting Nigeria’s defensive options.</p><!-- Ads Section Start -->

            </section>
            <!-- Ads Section Ends -->
<p>Austria-based Moses Usor, who scored on his Nigeria debut against Madagascar in Uyo on Sept. 25, was another expected addition to the squad. However, despite Chelle’s request for his release, LASK FC instructed the player not to travel to Russia.</p>
<p>The absence of several players highlights one of the recurring challenges facing international teams, particularly when fixtures fall outside periods when clubs are obliged to release players. National coaches can therefore find themselves preparing for important friendlies without some of their preferred selections.</p>
<p>For Nigeria, the situation also provides an opportunity to assess the strength of its wider player pool. With several established names unavailable, the Russia fixture could give fringe players valuable exposure at senior international level and allow Chelle to evaluate alternatives ahead of future competitive matches.</p>
<p>Suleiman Mubarak, invited from Slavia Prague in Czechia, was also unable to make the trip because his residence permit had not been secured. His absence adds another logistical setback to a squad already affected by injuries and club decisions.</p><!-- Ads Section Start -->

            </section>
            <!-- Ads Section Ends -->
<p>Nigeria’s reduced numbers will be tested against a Russian side that previously held the Super Eagles to a 1-1 draw in Moscow 16 months ago. The fixture therefore offers Chelle an opportunity to assess how his available players respond against a team with which Nigeria has already had a competitive encounter.</p>
<p>The late invitation of Ibraheem Ajasa of FC Rostov was expected to provide another option, with the player due to join the Super Eagles’ camp in Nizhny Novgorod on Sunday evening.</p>
<p>Despite the disruptions, 18 Super Eagles players are in Russia for the friendly. The available goalkeepers are Michael Atata of Ikorodu City, Samuel James of SJK FC in Finland and Stanley Nwabali of Chippa United in South Africa.</p>
<p>The defensive options include Kenneth Igboke of Enugu Rangers, Isaac James of Alverca FC in Portugal, Benjamin Fredricks of Brentford FC in England, Emmanuel Fernandez of Glasgow Rangers in Scotland and Abdullahi Bewene of FC Banik Ostrava in Czechia.</p><!-- Ads Section Start -->

            </section>
            <!-- Ads Section Ends -->
<p>In midfield, Nigeria will have Chibuzo Nwoke of Fulham FC, Stephen Michael of Vendsyssel FF, Igor Wilfred of Kristiansund FC and Aderemi Adeoye of Ikorodu City.</p>
<p>The forward line features Kelechi Iheanacho of Bursaspor FC, Moses Simon of Paris FC, Akor Adams of Venezia FC, Peter Edokpolor of SL Benfica, Abubakar Umar of FC Famalicao and Abdullahi Umar of Hradec Kralove.</p>
<p>Beyond the immediate result, the friendly offers Nigeria an important opportunity to measure the resilience of its player pool. The absence of key players means the match may provide Chelle with useful information about which alternatives can handle senior international football when regular starters are unavailable.</p>
<p>For the Super Eagles, managing injuries, club commitments and administrative challenges will remain important as the team builds toward future competitive fixtures. The Russia encounter will consequently be less about the availability of every first-choice player and more about how effectively Nigeria can use the resources at its disposal.</p>
